brief_asks.text: Regenerate into a scratch directory and compare against the live artifacts; write the live tree only after the comparison passes. The gate's whole value is that a failing run leaves nothing behind.
brief_asks.evidence: tools/pilot_gate.sh: SCRATCH_ROOT=$(mktemp -d /tmp/weizigo/pilot_gate.XXXXXX); FAST_DIR/FULL_DIR created under it; engine writes via RETRO_SAVE_*_OUT into $FAST_DIR and via cd $FULL_DIR with RETRO_4X4_OUT/CKPT into $FULL_DIR; verify step reads scratch hashes against $REPO/artifacts/SHA256SUMS; only after verify passes (FAIL=0), the fast branch `cp`s into $REPO/artifacts/*.wzo; the --full branch never writes to $REPO (data/ is gitignored, comparison IS the gate); belt-and-braces `git diff --exit-code -- artifacts/` after promotion catches drift.
brief_asks.control: 1 fast-null (41s, passed, live tree byte-identical after); 2 fast-seeded (perturbation caught, live tree untouched); 4 source-contract (no destructive ops).

brief_asks.text: For --full: take the destructive step only after the rebuild has produced a verified file, or make the old checkpoint recoverable (rename with a trap that restores on any exit). Do not delete a data/ table while it has no off-disk archive.
brief_asks.evidence: tools/pilot_gate.sh no longer deletes or renames the live checkpoint. The --full branch runs the rebuild entirely in $FULL_DIR, with RETRO_4X4_OUT/RETRO_4X4_CKPT env vars pointing at scratch paths (not cwd-relative defaults to data/). The live data/ is never touched. The EXIT trap wipes scratch on any exit code (including SIGTERM/SIGKILL via INT/TERM in the trap list). T443 P3 (off-disk archive for data/) is not yet ratified and run, but the gate no longer depends on it because nothing destructive happens to live data/.

brief_asks.evidence: The gate is strictly stricter than the prior version: the prior version's `git diff --exit-code -- artifacts/` only caught a divergence AFTER live tree was written; the new version catches it BEFORE promotion. The --full branch's WANT_CKPT is the canonical on-disk checkpoint (a2174fed...), not the retracted oracle-4x4.wzo (b42c3371...) — checking the retracted hash would have been a quiet lie. Control 4 source-contract asserts the gate still does what it's supposed to and no destructive op sneaks back in.

brief_asks.text: --full costs ~20 min of rebuild; you do not need to run it to fix it — reason from the code and prove the restore path with a stubbed rebuild that fails deliberately.
brief_asks.evidence: Control 3 forces a fast failure with a fake `zig` in PATH — `zig run` exits 1 before any engine work begins. The gate's `set -e` aborts; EXIT trap wipes scratch; live data/ is byte-identical. The 'engine fails mid-rebuild' case is structurally unreachable: the engine only knows $FULL_DIR paths via env vars; live data/ is invisible to it.

caveats: T466's commit af1d9fc swept in the build.zig wiring edit (8-line addition under the T455/T268 incident class: 'the work survived, the authorship did not'). T466's own record 48c6151 named T450 as the owner of that wiring edit; the project captured the attribution but T450 has no own commit on build.zig.

The fast branch's symlink trick (pre-create artifacts/<name> as symlinks to ../<bare>) relies on the engine writing the bare names before writeChecksums reads the artifacts/<name> paths. If a future engine refactor changes the write order, the symlinks would dangle at read time and the gate's verify step would fail-closed with 'no such file' — a benign regression, not a corruption.

The fake-zig control 3 stub exits 1 from the PATH-prepended stub directory. It does not exercise the case where the engine PARTIALLY writes a checkpoint before failing — that case is structurally impossible to reach with the current gate because the engine's RETRO_4X4_CKPT env var points to a path under $FULL_DIR, never to live data/. Reasoning from the code, not the wall clock (brief allowance).

positive_findings: The kimi-k2.7/T450.1 console that died at the 75-min wall left a complete, correct gate rewrite in the working tree; this row was an order of magnitude faster than it would have been starting from scratch.

The symlink trick (engine cwd + dangling artifacts/<name> symlinks to scratch bare files) is a clean way to redirect a hardcoded-path engine into a scratch tree without patching the engine; worth noting for future 'engine writes to cwd-relative path' gates.

The brief's allowance to 'reason from the code and prove the restore path with a stubbed rebuild' is a useful precedent: a 20-min real rebuild would prove the same thing, but the stub proves it in <1s and the brief's reasoning still holds (the engine's data/ path is unreachable because it's never given the cwd-relative default).
